name: Jerimoth
overview: Jerimoth was a male Levite who served as an overseer of the consecrated things under Conaniah, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 31:13. His role was significant within the Levitical duties related to the sacred offerings and temple service. There are no additional notes providing further details about his life or ministry.
namesAndTitles: The name Jerimoth means "swollen or obese." This proper name is noted in 2 Chronicles 31:13 and does not appear to have been given directly by God. The meaning of the name is straightforward and does not carry additional theological significance in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Jerimoth is identified as a descendant of Levi, indicating his tribal lineage as a Levite. Beyond this tribal affiliation, Scripture does not record any further family relationships for Jerimoth.
scriptureSignificance: Jerimoth's importance in Scripture lies in his appointed responsibility over the consecrated things in the temple service, demonstrating the organized and faithful stewardship of God's house during the reign of King Hezekiah. His role under Conaniah highlights the careful administration of temple duties by Levites, which was crucial for maintaining proper worship and honoring God. This service reflects the biblical emphasis on order and dedication in serving the Lord.
